correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs uniform Cayley-tree path completions via rooted-forest determinants, weighted determinants for root and nonroot degrees, all boundary cases and exact path mixing. The leaf-ordering proof and stochastic crossing are algebraic. A uniform second-order generating-function expansion plus Rayleigh tail domination proves the fixed-threshold covariance limit; independent exhaustive Prüfer enumeration through n=8 and 11,422 exact-or-numerical assertions passed. Numerical tests alone are not treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The naturally motivated nonendpoint local degree versus global marked-pair distance has a distinct dependence mechanism from endpoint degree. The exact law and its second-order cancellation show a substantive structural boundary: nonleaf probability rises strictly with distance, but the covariance with any fixed degree-at-least-four event is eventually negative with explicit sharp coefficient. This goes beyond a trivial conservation-of-degree mean or isolated numerical computation.
